method: Static reverse engineering only; no sample code was executed. Full atomscan slow/local scans and cleave facts on all originals, decrypted stages and relevant archive members; Capstone instruction/call tracing, Rizin PE inspection, dnfile/dncil CIL decoding, AES/XOR/Base64 and RC4 configuration recovery. Classifier probabilities and sandbox names did not determine verdicts.
counting: Hostile/suspicious counts deduplicate trait IDs across all analysis units, including archive members and decoded stages. Per-unit counts retain inherited findings. No finding was removed or downgraded.

samples.identification: StormAttack DLL-injection loader and packet-tasked DDoS module
evidence: Outer PE entry 0x402674 reaches dispatch at 0x401cb0. Configuration dword at VA 0x404120 is 3; its selected branch calls 0x401900 then 0x401390. Registry key and value-name strings in that branch are damaged random text, not a valid Active Setup/StubPath installation. Do not claim functioning Active Setup persistence.

Other retained code branches extract resource DLL/101 via 0x402460 and write it using CreateFileA/WriteFile. 0x401150 creates a native host, allocates/writes a DLL path remotely, resolves LoadLibraryA and calls CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d. Code at 0x401fd0 copies/hides its image and has auto-start service installation; this is code capability, not proof the configured branch executed.

At 0x401260 the code opens a configured HKLM key, deletes lowercase servicedll and writes REG_EXPAND_SZ, size 128, through RegSetValueExA at 0x40133e. The configured key is damaged, so the corrected neutral observation makes no successful service hijack claim.

0x401390 obtains its own module and short path, reads COMSPEC, builds /c del and calls CreateProcessA at 0x4014b8 with flags including suspended startup, then resumes it. Retained hostile cleanup describes this code, not runtime success.

Resource begins at file offset 0x8060, size 0x9c00. The embedded DLL places code in a non-executable .data section and has no NX compatibility flag. Entry 0x1000741a is real CRT/DLL code. The packet record handler at 0x10006b45 calls recv, copies a 0x528-byte record, dispatches its command and attack subtype, and calls flood routines. At 0x100022b6 WSASocketA receives raw UDP arguments; 0x10002353 initializes a count of twelve, sendto at 0x1000236b repeats, then sleeps and loops until the shared stop flag.

Shutdown tasks lead to functions around 0x10006549: OpenProcessToken, LookupPrivilegeValueA for SeShutdownPrivilege, AdjustTokenPrivileges with enabled privilege, and ExitWindowsEx at 0x1000659b. This confirms the retained privileged-shutdown finding.

A download-and-launch task branch exists at 0x100067c2, called from task 5 at 0x10006bb1. Its CreateProcess argument sequence near 0x10006907 is overwritten with non-code bytes; no new static claim of a valid linked download-execute chain was added. Registry target corruption and partial task damage limit runtime success claims, not the concrete flood implementation.

Storm Ser DLL version identity corroborates StormAttack, but packet tasking and raw packet floods independently establish hostile intent. No WannaCry encryption or Remcos agent exists in this original despite its collector-assigned basename. The supplied tria.ge URL could not be opened; the verdict rests on bytes.
samples.marker_line: StormAttack: packet floods and hidden injector; ServiceDLL case fix

samples.identification: AES/XOR PowerShell launcher, .NET process hollower, native Remcos agent
evidence: Outer s111.ps1 normalizes Base64 then AES-256-CBC decrypts with its embedded key and IV, constructs ScriptBlock from decrypted UTF-8 and invokes it. Decrypted stage is 1,875,213 bytes.

Start-BeaconCycle checks aspnet_compiler process liveness every five seconds. When absent it Base64-decodes a blob, applies repeating UTF-8 XOR, Base64-decodes the result, loads the .NET assembly from bytes, resolves FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER and invokes it with a Framework v4.0.30319 aspnet_compiler.exe path plus the decimal-array native PE.

CIL LAUNCHER at RVA 0x207c retries qASnOg2Lc up to five times. The initialized delegate array sequences process creation with flags 0x08000004 (suspended and no window), PE header parsing, thread-context acquisition, remote allocation/header/section writes, PEB image-base write, saved entry-point rewrite and resume. Failure cleanup terminates the created process. RVAs 0x2548, 0x2640 and 0x26ac copy sections, write the PEB image base and replace the context entry slot.

Native Remcos has product banners and an RC4-encrypted SETTINGS resource at file 0x7e9cc, length 749. First byte is the 247-byte key length; decrypting the remaining resource yields 58 separator-delimited fields and controller toolstally.duckdns.org:7030. No option-index assumptions were used to claim enabled recording.

At native VA 0x40c0e2 the installed hook type is WH_KEYBOARD_LL (13), zero thread ID, a real callback and current-module handle. The callback and key record formatting use keyboard translation and bracketed special-key strings. Existing recording-start status strings and foreground-window APIs support keylogging context. The existing generic hook classifier omitted this x86 setup variant, preventing four accurate hostile consumer findings.

0x40d50d opens the clipboard and calls GetClipboardData(CF_UNICODETEXT) at 0x40d51c. Caller 0x40d547 reads that result, checks for changed/nonempty text, brackets it with copied-text/end-of-clipboard labels at 0x40d5d8..0x40d5e5 and passes the record to the recorder at 0x40d629. Another remote command branch reads Unicode clipboard text at 0x41af2d.

Native code imports and calls waveInOpen, waveInPrepareHeader, waveInAddBuffer and waveInStart; screen capture code calls BitBlt at 0x41d625. Browser cleanup and file-transfer/hollowing implementations corroborate retained Remcos findings. CoGetObject elevation path around 0x408493 builds an elevation moniker and reaches the CMSTPLUA interface. These are capabilities, not assertions that every configurable feature was active.

The encrypted, hidden image-transplant chain and configured external remote controller tip the balance to MALICIOUS. Authorized deployment context for the commercial Remcos product is absent; the verdict is not based on the product name alone.
samples.marker_line: Remcos loader: encrypted hollowing and input capture; fix hook coverage

samples.identification: @craft-native/ios 0.0.345 iOS project builder and Swift bridge templates
evidence: Manifest identifies @craft-native/ios 0.0.345, author Chris Breuer, MIT license, craft-native/craft monorepo packages/ios, and the craft-ios CLI. It declares no install lifecycle hook or dependencies. forager recovered the pinned npm registry tarball with provenance in scratch; its SHA-256 is byte-identical to the original ce2213dd05567540ff341e74fabd16e9c7f97bf551cc9c6139609c5a2663db87.

dist/cli.js dispatches explicit user build/init/test commands. dist/index.js init writes a configured Xcode project, Swift templates, plist, entitlements and offline assets; build copies chosen content and invokes the platform build tools. runPostGenerateHook validates user-supplied command/argv, then calls Bun.spawnSync with inherited environment and explicit build-context variables. Test helpers compile a local Swift mutation validator and run a selected binary against test input; they do not fetch hidden payloads.

Native bundle gzip compression, rmSync of generated output, sips image conversion, simulator tools and shell templates have documented build purposes. GitHub workflows grant contents:write to publish release artifacts, reference configured signing secrets and chmod the Gradle wrapper; these accurate notable traits were retained. No fetched-dependency false positive was found.

CraftApp.swift userContentController checks message.frameInfo.securityOrigin with isTrustedOrigin before dispatch. Camera, speech, microphone, keychain, contacts and location features are configured flags, generally disabled in DEFAULT_CONFIG, and use platform permission APIs. These are an application bridge surface, not evidence of covert surveillance.

CraftCrashReporter.swift configure requires crashReporting settings and a nonempty key, otherwise enabled remains false. It stages JSON crash/session reports and flushes them via POST to the configured service (default https://bughq.org). Native memory reads support stack/crash reporting. CraftNativeFiles serves app-selected downloads, sandbox files and picker operations.

CraftApp.swift line 1429 fetches a selected image through URLSession.shared.data(from:), checks response status, builds UIImage and caches it. The new notable HTTP fetch rule covers this previously missed operation without classifying it as hostile.

BENIGN follows from the inspected, coherent builder/bridge implementation and identical published artifact, not a clean trait scan. There is no deployment-specific evidence of abuse or a substituted payload. The classifier still assigns 1.0 to CraftApp.swift, CraftCrashReporter.swift, CraftNativeActions.swift and CraftNativeFiles.swift and propagates that to the archive. This is a remaining classifier false positive, not a reason to suppress their accurately detected capabilities.
samples.marker_line: Craft iOS builder: documented build and bridge APIs; add HTTP fetch

changes.change: Include the existing x86-global-low-level-keyboard-hook-setup atom in windows-keyboard-hook-install. All prior alternatives and exclusions remain. This propagates a verified keyboard hook into existing recording and multi-source detections rather than adding duplicate family signatures.
changes.consumers: Audited all exact windows-keyboard-hook-install YAML consumers. Added findings were individually reviewed; they describe recorded keys, clipboard logging, audio APIs, hook/thread context, or neutral window-title/key recording. No added finding asserts audio upload or enabled recording configuration.

changes.change: Match the Windows registry value name ServiceDLL without case sensitivity. The x86 instruction layout, IAT bindings, same value pointer, 128-byte size and .text bounds are unchanged. The reviewed original uses lowercase servicedll. This is a value-write observation, not a claim that a valid service key is targeted.
Add notable Swift URLSession.shared.data(from:) call matching. The parsed call node excludes comments, quoted examples, unrelated objects and the data(for:) request overload.

coverage: Uppercase and lowercase ServiceDLL positive controls
Wrong value name and wrong called IAT near misses
Global keyboard hook positive and WH_MOUSE_LL near miss
Swift async URL fetch positive, request overload, comment/string examples and unrelated object near misses
